classification.difficultyReason: The unknown is the speed rather than the angle. The student eliminates t with a given angle, which gives a linear equation in 1/V². Part (a) adds a non-zero launch height, and part (b) uses a sec² substitution. Each part is routine but needs setup choices.

content.prompt: Find the initial speed of the projectile in each case. Give your answers to 1 d.p. Use $g=10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A ball is thrown at $45^\circ$ above the horizontal from the top of a $20\text{ m}$ cliff and lands $20\text{ m}$ from the base of the cliff.

answer.worked:
Let $V$ be the initial speed. Take the point of projection as the origin, so the ground is at $y=-20$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=V\cos45^\circ\,t\\y&=V\sin45^\circ\,t-5t^2\end{align*}$$
At landing, $x=20$ and $y=-20$.
$$\begin{align*}20&=V\cos45^\circ\,t\\t&=\frac{20\sqrt2}{V}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the vertical equation:
$$\begin{align*}-20&=V\sin45^\circ\left(\frac{20\sqrt2}{V}\right)-5\left(\frac{20\sqrt2}{V}\right)^2\\-20&=20-\frac{4000}{V^2}\\\frac{4000}{V^2}&=40\\V^2&=100\\V&=10.0\text{ m s}^{-1}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A ball is thrown from level ground at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal and passes through a point $30\text{ m}$ away horizontally and $5\text{ m}$ above the ground.

answer.worked:
Let $V$ be the initial speed. Take the point of projection as the origin.
$$\begin{align*}x&=V\cos30^\circ\,t\\y&=V\sin30^\circ\,t-5t^2\end{align*}$$
At the point, $x=30$ and $y=5$.
$$\begin{align*}30&=V\cos30^\circ\,t\\t&=\frac{20\sqrt3}{V}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the vertical equation:
$$\begin{align*}5&=V\sin30^\circ\left(\frac{20\sqrt3}{V}\right)-5\left(\frac{20\sqrt3}{V}\right)^2\\5&=10\sqrt3-\frac{6000}{V^2}\\\frac{6000}{V^2}&=10\sqrt3-5\\V^2&=\frac{6000}{10\sqrt3-5}\\&\approx487.0\\V&\approx22.1\text{ m s}^{-1}\end{align*}$$
